key_insight: CCL alternates teacher calibration on source feedback with student learning on target questions to suppress teacher bias and drive the student toward the oracle policy without any target-domain reward labels.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical distillation recipe for deploying smaller LLMs under distribution shift, where target feedback is unavailable but bias transfer from a stronger teacher must be controlled.
method: Calibrate the teacher using reward feedback from source-domain questions only.
Use the calibrated teacher to generate token-level branches and train the student on target-domain questions.
Feed the updated student back into the next calibration step to jointly improve teacher reliability and student policy.
evidence_signal: In an autoregressive policy analysis, the paper proves the student’s average KL divergence to the oracle student converges to zero at a polynomial rate and shows direct matching can remain biased away from the oracle.
watch_item: The guarantees are theoretical and depend on iterative calibration/optimization assumptions, so real-world gains may be sensitive to branching design, reward quality, and optimization stability.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
